title: Trichoderma swollenin activates AtABCB5-dependent auxin efflux to promote plant development.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC marks the paper not open access, with no PMCID, no supplement, no NCBI links (GEO, SRA or BioProject), no Zenodo or Dryad record and no accession numbers. The only text-mined accessions are two antibody RRIDs (research resource identifiers).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything comes from the abstract: a mechanistic study of one fungal protein (ThSWO, a swollenin) binding one plant auxin transporter (AtABCB5), using binding assays, phosphorylation-site mutants, auxin efflux assays and lateral root phenotypes.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset was found in any repository, and the paper is paywalled with no PMC copy. Checked through Europe PMC and NCBI links, not by opening files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table of labelled examples exists. The outcomes are small-scale experimental readouts (efflux, root counts) for a handful of mutants.

a3_inputs_present.note: There are no inputs at scale. The study covers one protein pair plus a few interface substitutions.

a5_enough_rows.note: A mechanistic single-interaction study, probably tens of conditions, far below 400 rows. Not verified, because there is no data file.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No download to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Readouts would be physical measurements, but there are too few of them to use.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible: the paper characterises one fungal effector–host transporter interaction and deposits no dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use fungal protein and plant transporter sequences to predict whether they bind and promote root growth.
plain_idea.train_on: The considered inputs were pairs of a fungal effector and a host transporter (wild type and interface mutants). The number of examples is unknown, probably tens.
plain_idea.predict: Binding strength or lateral-root promotion, as measured in the paper's binding and root-phenotype assays.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could guide engineering of beneficial fungal proteins for crops. But one interaction with a few mutants cannot train a model.

label_elsewhere.sources: None identified; not searched, since the project was rejected at Part A.
label_elsewhere.why: The label exists only for this one protein pair, so no extra labelled data is available.

ml_idea: None viable. This is a mechanistic wet-lab study of one effector–transporter pair, with no deposited tabular or omics data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because there is no dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check for any GEO/SRA/PRIDE deposit linked to PMID 42492507. None was found.

verdict_reason: A paywalled mechanistic study of a single fungal effector–host transporter interaction. No deposited dataset was found and there are only a few experimental conditions, so A1 (downloadable) and A5 (enough rows) fail.
